# Jubilees Chapter 42 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** The silver cup trap; Joseph's identity revealed; family reunited

---

**42:1** Jacob was still in Canaan. In the second year of the famine, he and his sons made the journey down to Egypt.

**42:2** Joseph had ordered his steward to plant a silver cup in Benjamin's sack. When the brothers left the city, Joseph's men caught up with them and searched. They found the cup in Benjamin's pack.

**42:3** The brothers were hauled back in front of Joseph. "What were you thinking?" he demanded. "Did you think I wouldn't find out? A man like me can read omens."

**42:4** Judah stepped forward. "What can we possibly say, sir? God himself has exposed us. We're all your slaves now — all of us, including the one who had the cup."

**42:5** "No," Joseph said. "Only the man with the cup stays. The rest of you go home to your father."

**42:6** Judah came right up to Joseph: "Please, sir — can I say something? Don't be angry. You have the power of Pharaoh himself."

**42:7** He poured out the whole story — their father Jacob, ancient and fragile; the promise made to bring Benjamin home; what his father's death would look like if Benjamin didn't return.

**42:8** Joseph couldn't hold it together any longer. "Everyone out!" he ordered. The room cleared.

**42:9** He broke down sobbing. His brothers heard it. He told them: "I'm Joseph."

**42:10** "I'm Joseph — the brother you sold to Egypt. Don't be afraid. Don't feel guilty. God is the one who sent me here — not you. He was ahead of all of us, working to keep this family alive."

**42:11** He went around and hugged and kissed every one of them, weeping. Then they all talked.

**42:12** Joseph sent word to Pharaoh: "My father and brothers have arrived from Canaan, with all their livestock and possessions. They're settled in Goshen."

---

*PNEUMA notes: The revelation scene is one of the most emotionally powerful in all of ancient literature. Jubilees preserves it in compressed but faithful form. Joseph's "God sent me ahead of you" (v.10) is the theological core of the entire Joseph cycle — Providence working through human betrayal.*
